content: Have you ever wondered what the Earth looks like from space? Imagine you are an astronaut floating far, far away in a spaceship, looking down at our home. What colors do you think you would see shining brightly?
Why do you think our Earth looks mostly blue from space? Is it painted blue, or is there something special covering it?

content.title: The Blue Planet
content.description: An animation showing our Earth covered mostly by water.

content: The Reveal! The Earth looks blue because most of it is covered in water! The blue parts are oceans and seas, while the green and brown parts are the solid land where we build our houses and grow our food.

Earth (Prithvi): The beautiful planet we live on. In ancient Indian texts like the Vedas, Earth is respected as 'Bhumi' or 'Prithvi Mata' (Mother Earth) because she provides us with food, water, and shelter.

question: Why does the Earth look mostly blue from space?
options: Because the sky is painted blue
Because most of it is covered in water
Because blue is the best color

content: Reflection Time: Think about the land around your house. Is it flat like a playground, or high up like a hill? How would your day be different if you lived on top of a snowy mountain?

Connection: Just like your school has different rooms (classroom, playground, library), our Earth has different shapes of land. We call these Landforms! There are high mountains, deep valleys, flat plains, and sandy deserts.
Mastery Challenge: Draw a big circle in your notebook to represent the Earth. Color most of it blue for the oceans, and the rest green and brown for the land. Mark a tiny star to show where you live!

Bring a globe to the class and let students spin it. Ask them to close their eyes and point a finger at the spinning globe. When it stops, have them check if their finger landed on water or land. This builds a strong intuitive understanding of water-to-land ratio.
Students often think rivers and lakes make up most of the Earth's water. Remember to clarify that oceans and seas hold almost all of the blue color we see from space!
